newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania launches inquiry into Azomures selloff.
newsitem.headline: Romania launches inquiry into Azomures selloff.

text.p: Romania's government has asked the country's main privatisation agency to halt a contract on the sell-off of a majority stake in listed Azomures pending police investigations, an official said on Wednesday.
"We have filed documents on Azomures' privatisation to the police for analysis after we noted irregulaties," Economic Reform Council official Liviu Lefter told Reuters.
"We also asked the State Ownership Fund (FPS) to halt the contract for the time being," he added.
The FPS, the former main holder of Azomures, a fertiliser maker traded on the bourse's first tier, sold 51 percent of the company last Tuesday. Azomures' capital is 209.5 billion lei ($30.8 million).

The sale, to Romanian trading company Euro Trading Chemicals SRL, was announced a day later. Stock brokers and bourse officials have attacked the deal on the grounds that rules on the transparency of listed stocks had been breached.
"If the police notes irregularities, the case may go to justice," Lefter said.
He said alleged irregularities included the FPS' failure to get National Privatisation Agency (ANP) clearance for the sale and to contact the bourse for Azomures' shareholder structure.
"Euro Trading bought the stake in association with Azomures staff, but who got how much was never disclosed," Lefter said.
Azomures manager Vasile Urdea told Reuters last week that company employees would get 10 percent of the stake.
Euro Trading officials could not be contacted since the sale last week.
"There was also an irregularity in selecting one of the two bids, with the FPS giving more weight -- about 65 percent -- to commitments other than price," Lefter said.
The second bidder for Azomures was local trader Omnimpex Chemicals SA, who said its price bid had been 140 billion lei higher. Omnimpex has appealed to FPS against tender results.
The FPS said it had sold Euro Trading the Azomures shares at 90,000 lei each, without giving an overall purchasing price.
